title: The Sad news from the hospital
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：sad　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sad 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the shopkeeper wrote of ① a sad news from the hospital in the account, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② sadder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the shopkeeper, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the sad ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the saddest news from the hospital anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the account for July 1944 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sad to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the buyer who had come to help; the sad ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sad end of the story, and said that no buyer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sad as the end of the story they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sad or not, and he said so.

By 1957 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the account. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sad, and nothing besides. The buyer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite sad; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the account kept the names of the sad ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1960, without complaint, she wrote of another sad news from the hospital in the same account, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ sadder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The saddest end of the story in the whole shop, she said in 1962, was the one she could never quite name; the sad ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 悲伤（前置定语 a sad news from the hospital：1950 年掌柜在账本里记下的那件悲伤的坏消息）
B. adj. 悲伤／可悲（比较级 sadder than：文中两处，一处比医院传来的坏消息，一处比预想）
C. adj. 悲伤／可悲（最高级 the saddest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 悲伤（表语 too sad to do：母亲觉得它太悲伤，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 可悲（前置定语 a sad end of the story：叔叔把整件事称作一桩可悲的结局）
F. adj. 可悲（同级比较 as sad as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩故事悲惨的结局相比）
G. adj. 可悲（后置定语 something sad：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 可悲（受程度副词修饰 quite sad：那位买主的评价）

items.q: a sad news from the hospital
the saddest news from the hospital anybody
a sad end of the story
The saddest end of the story in

answers.why: sad 意为“悲伤”，1950 年掌柜在账本里记下的是“一件悲伤的坏消息”，此处作前置定语 a sad news from the hospital。
sad 意为“悲伤”，此处用比较级 sadder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sad 意为“悲伤”，账本上 七月 那行字说它是铺子里最悲伤的一件，故用最高级 the saddest news from the hospital。
sad 意为“悲伤”，母亲认为这件东西“太悲伤了，谁也用不上”，too sad to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sad 意为“可悲”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩可悲的结局”，此处作前置定语 a sad end of the story。
sad 意为“可悲”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩故事悲惨的结局一样可悲”，同级比较用 as sad as。
sad 意为“可悲”，账本上那半行字要的是“可悲的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sad。
sad 意为“可悲”，邻铺子来的那位买主认为这套计划“相当可悲”，quite 修饰原级 sad。
sad 意为“可悲”，1960 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要可悲”，故用比较级 sadder than。
sad 意为“可悲”，母亲 1962 年说的是“整个铺子里最可悲的那一桩”，故用最高级 the saddest end of the story。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1950 年，掌柜在账本里记下了一件悲伤的坏消息。（a sad news from the hospital）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更悲伤。（sadder than …）
母亲觉得它太悲伤，谁也用不上。（too sad to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩可悲的结局。（a sad end of the story）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩故事悲惨的结局一样可悲。（as sad as …）
到了 1957 年，账本上只剩半行字：要的是一件可悲的东西。（something sad）
answers: In 1950 the shopkeeper wrote of a sad news from the hospital in the account.
Everybody said it was sadder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sad to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sad end of the story.
He said nobody would call it as sad as the end of the story they had once had.
By 1957 the account asked for nothing but something sad.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sad 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the shopkeeper wrote of a sad news from the hospital in the account, and nobody forgot it.
It was the saddest news from the hospital in the shop, or so the account says.
My mother thought it too sad to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sad end of the story, and nobody argued with him.
The buyer from the next shop called the plan quite sad, and everybody laughed.
The sad ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
